item.content:encoded:
Cheers! 4504 was kinda the "show-don't-tell" of this, although there was more to that too. This was something I wrote in response to a lot of the criticisms of that, who said the shrinks in that were "incompetent". The point is they aren't really incompetent, its just their first priority isn't helping the skips, its containing them, which results in inferior care. Though I'm definitely going to remember this feedback, maybe do some more show-don't-tell of this in the future.

For now tho, my next project is going to be a Sigma-3 tale.

item.title: Re: Novote
item.content:encoded:
While its true the Foundation can and does help skips when they might need assistance, that isn't their first priority. The thing I was trying to get across with this tale is that a skip's psychiatrist's goal is going to be to contain them first and help them second, which is going to result in worse care for the skip.

Thanks for the feedback tho!

The thing is, I really liked SCP-4504. Some of my problems here were also reflected by fieldstone, where they're just too open about the way things are. If the whole "we counsel them so containment is easier but we don't give a shit" was shown rather than told, this could easily be a strong upvote from me.

item.title: Novote
item.content:encoded:
It's well-written, and it does get its point across, but it's a fairly bleak take on humanoid containment. To me there isn't a good justification for why they just want idle prisoners instead of actively helping their mental health. The latter is valuable when it aids containment obviously, but for some kinds of anomalies it can also help them manage or even neutralize their anomalous traits.

There are some humanoids who turned themselves in because they need care, because they need assistance to live with their anomalous traits. This doesn't reflect that at all. It's just "all scips are angry and want to breach containment", and the solution is apparently to ignore the root cause and hope more don't breach later.

Edit: I saw your changes, and while it does make sense in the crueler varieties of the Foundation, I'm sticking with my current vote. I will say I like how much conversation this tale generated, it's definitely valuable in that regard.
